issues.body: The test asserts that the output contains actions for three providers, but restoring `if not prov_records: continue` immediately after `prov_records` is built cannot skip any of them: `providers` was constructed from the same `records` list using the same provider value, so `prov_records` is non-empty for every loop iteration. Consequently the exact mutation this row and both surrounding comment blocks claim will turn red instead survives. The row may test a broader output invariant, but it is not evidence for deleting this unreachable branch and the stated mutation result is false.
issues.fix_hint: Run the claimed reintroduction mutant and report it honestly as equivalent/unreachable. Remove or correct the claims that this row kills a reintroduced emptiness guard. Keep the output-invariant test only if it is justified as protection against a distinct reachable provider-skip mutation, and name that concrete mutation separately.
issues.title: New self-test cannot detect reintroduction of the deleted guard

verdict.summary: The unreachable guard can be removed safely, but the added self-test is presented as mutation evidence that it cannot provide. Reintroducing the exact deleted `if not prov_records: continue` leaves the new row green, because each iterated provider is derived from `records` and therefore always has at least one matching `prov_records` entry. The source comments repeatedly claim the opposite, so the change's marquee validation claim is unsound.
